test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 27 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Under the NPS Vatsalya scheme, subsequent contribution of what minimum amount is required per annum with no maximum limit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1,000**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** minimum annual contribution to the NPS Vatsalya scheme is ₹1,000**, with no maximum limit. 
 
• The NPS Vatsalya scheme **is a financial investment that parents or guardians can make for their minor children. **
 
• The** scheme helps provide financial support for childre**n until they are able to earn and invest on their own. 
 
• The scheme **offers flexibility for self-contributions. **
 
• The scheme **can be opened through various Points of Presence (PoPs) regulated by PFRDA. **
 
• The scheme can be opened online through the eNPS platform of NPS Trust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of the Vatsalya Schem**e

 
 
• Give top priority to children in all administrative activities under the Mission.
 
• Ensure t**he child's best interests when planning and delivering projects,** focusing on their right to grow in a supportive family environment.
 
• Safeguard children's rights to survival, development, protection, and participation.
 
• Establish **crucial services and enhance emergency suppor**t, both within families and communities, as well as institutional care, counseling, and support services at various levels.
 
• Promote** inter-sectoral responses, coordination, and collaboration with allied systems to ensure seamless service delivery for children.**
 
• **Strengthen child protection at the family and community levels by empowering them to identify risks** and take preventive measures.
 
• Encourage private sector partnerships within the legal framework for supporting children.
 
• Monitor progress using well-defined objectives and outcomes.
 
• **Involve Panchayats and Municipal Local Bodies at the village and urban cluster levels to assess issues,** implement appropriate interventions, and monitor progress in building a robust safety net for children.
